yes.label: Yes
yes.description: Stated in the vendor's own public documentation.

partial.label: Partial
partial.description: True with a caveat, spelled out in the cell.

no.label: No
no.description: Not offered, per the vendor’s own documentation. A No is not a criticism: it can be the right call for what the product is.

na.label: n/a
na.description: The question does not apply to this kind of product.

fact.label: Documented
fact.description: A value from the vendor's own public pages.

vendor-claim.label: Vendor claim
vendor-claim.description: A marketing figure we could not check independently.

not-verified.label: Not verified
not-verified.description: We could not confirm it either way. Do not read it as a No.

not-documented.label: Not documented
not-documented.description: We read the vendor’s own docs and they do not say. Ask the vendor.

not-disclosed.label: Not disclosed
not-disclosed.description: The vendor’s own pages do not name who operates it.

judgement.label: Our judgement
judgement.description: Opinion, labelled as such. Not a documented fact.

criteria.label: Primary product
criteria.help: What the vendor mainly sells.

criteria.label: Ownership
criteria.help: Who owns or operates it. A change of owner can change pricing and the roadmap.

criteria.label: Exchanges covered
criteria.help: Venue coverage as the vendor documents it. Marketing figures we could not check are marked as vendor claims.

criteria.label: Full instrument universe per venue
criteria.help: Whether every listed instrument on a covered venue is collected, not only the large pairs. A partial universe biases cross-sectional research.

criteria.label: Delisted / expired instruments retained
criteria.help: Whether delisted and expired instruments stay queryable. Without them a backtest carries survivorship bias.

criteria.label: Earliest data available
criteria.help: The first date the vendor documents data for.

criteria.label: How much history you actually get
criteria.help: How much history a plan includes, which is often less than the archive holds.

criteria.label: Local / receive timestamp
criteria.help: When the vendor's collector received each message. You need it to model latency and avoid look-ahead.

criteria.label: Aggregations computed on local-timestamp ordering
criteria.help: Whether bars and metrics are built in receive-time order, which matches what you could have known at the time.

criteria.label: Data restated after publication
criteria.help: Whether published history gets revised. Silent revisions break reproducible backtests; versioned ones do not.

criteria.label: Tick trades
criteria.help: Every trade print.

criteria.label: L2 book, incremental updates
criteria.help: Incremental order book updates that let you rebuild the book.

criteria.label: L2 book, snapshots
criteria.help: Periodic snapshots of the book at a fixed depth.

criteria.label: L3 / market-by-order
criteria.help: Order-level data.

criteria.label: Options
criteria.help: Options data of any kind.

criteria.label: Bars: OHLCV, VWAP / TWAP
criteria.help: Ready-made price bars.

criteria.label: Order flow and flow toxicity
criteria.help: Taker buy and sell volume, signed delta, CVD and toxicity measures such as VPIN.

criteria.label: Trade size distribution
criteria.help: Volume broken down by trade size.

criteria.label: Market impact: Amihud, Kyle lambda
criteria.help: Price-impact measures such as Amihud illiquidity and Kyle's lambda.

criteria.label: Execution slippage
criteria.help: Measured or estimated execution cost against the best price.

criteria.label: Realized volatility and jump structure
criteria.help: Realized volatility, and jump measures such as bipower variation.

criteria.label: Tick and run structure
criteria.help: Uptick and downtick counts and run lengths.

criteria.label: L1 spread, depth, imbalance
criteria.help: Top-of-book spread, size and imbalance series.

criteria.label: L2 depth and imbalance by level
criteria.help: Depth and imbalance at fixed book levels or depth bands.

criteria.label: Derivatives: funding, OI, basis, mark vs index
criteria.help: Funding, open interest, basis, and mark against index price.

criteria.label: Aggregation intervals offered
criteria.help: The bar and metric intervals on offer.

criteria.label: Breadth of derived catalogue
criteria.help: How much derived data the vendor publishes.

criteria.label: Compute you still have to do yourself
criteria.help: Our judgement of how much computation stays with you.

criteria.label: Delivery format
criteria.help: How the data reaches you.

criteria.label: Rate limits or volume caps
criteria.help: Request, transfer or volume limits.

criteria.label: Friction on a full historical backfill
criteria.help: What slows down pulling the full history.

criteria.label: How the pricing works
criteria.help: How the price is structured.

criteria.label: What the price gates
criteria.help: What the plans restrict. Read this before comparing the prices below it.

criteria.label: Full historical data access on a monthly subscription
criteria.help: Whether a month-to-month plan unlocks the whole history, or full history needs yearly billing or a contract.

criteria.label: Entry price
criteria.help: The cheapest listed way in.

criteria.label: What you get at the entry price
criteria.help: What the cheapest plan includes.

criteria.label: Usable without an API key
criteria.help: Whether you can try the data before creating a key.

criteria.label: Self-serve signup
criteria.help: Whether you can sign up and pay without talking to sales.

criteria.label: Best suited to
criteria.help: Our judgement of the job each vendor fits best.

criteria.label: Main gotchas
criteria.help: Our judgement: what to know before buying.

sources.title: Tardis.dev pricing table and billing FAQ
sources.note: Pricing is subscription type x data plan x billing interval; from $350/month (Academic, Perpetuals or Options, quarterly or yearly) to $6,000/month (Business, All Exchanges)

sources.title: Tardis.dev billing FAQ: history by billing interval
sources.note: Yearly billing: Business gets all history since 2019-03-30, Academic, Solo and Pro get 4 years; quarterly 12 months; monthly 4 months

sources.title: Tardis.dev billing FAQ: what each plan includes
sources.note: CSV downloads on all plans; Pro and Business add raw replay API, tardis-machine, instruments metadata

sources.title: Tardis.dev billing FAQ: source IPs and free trial
sources.note: One source IP per API key at a time on Academic, Solo and Pro, multiple on Business; one-month free trial with 7 to 14 days of recent data

sources.title: Tardis.dev API rate limits
sources.note: 3,000 req/min Solo/Academic/Pro, 9,000 Business; transfer 20 TB monthly to 240 TB yearly (Business 60 TB to 720 TB). One key on Solo/Academic/Pro, up to 10 on Business; all keys share the account quota. Request limits count raw replay API calls; official clients call it in parallel, so concurrent replay sessions hit the limit quickly; transfer caps per billing interval, no usage meter documented

sources.title: Tardis.dev data FAQ
